```plato
    // How many endpoints of the strut land on `node` once the cell is tiled:
    // zero when a neighbouring cell owns the strut, otherwise 0, 1 or 2. Both
    // endpoints count when a strut runs from a node to its own periodic image,
    // which is exactly what a cube edge of the simple cubic cell does.
    StrutIncidence(self: LatticeUnitCell, s: LatticeStrut, node: Point3D): Integer
    {
        var a = self.StrutEndpointA(s);
        var b = self.StrutEndpointB(s);
        return CellOwnsStrut(a, b).Not
            ? 0
            : (SameLatticeNode(a, node) ? 1 : 0) + (SameLatticeNode(b, node) ? 1 : 0);
    }

    // The coordination number of a node in the INFINITE tiling of this cell:
    // how many struts meet there once the cell repeats, which is generally more
    // than the number of struts touching that node inside one cell.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordination_number)
    NodeValence(self: LatticeUnitCell, node: ItemIndex): Integer
    {
        var p = self.Nodes[node.Value];
        return self.Struts.Reduce(0, (acc, s) => acc + self.StrutIncidence(s, p));
    }

    // The coordination number of every node of the cell, parallel to Nodes.
    // Nodes that are periodic images of one another report the same number.
    NodeValences(self: LatticeUnitCell): Array<Integer>
        => self.Nodes.Count.MapRange(i => self.NodeValence(ItemIndex(i)));

    // The length of a strut in normalized cell coordinates: multiply by the cell
    // size to get a world length in a cell that is a cube.
    NormalizedStrutLength(self: LatticeUnitCell, s: LatticeStrut): Number
        => self.StrutEndpointA(s).Distance(self.StrutEndpointB(s));

    // How many struts one interior cell contributes to the tiling: the cell's
    // struts less the ones its neighbours own.
    OwnedStrutCount(self: LatticeUnitCell): Integer
        => self.Struts.Reduce(0, (acc, s) =>
            acc + (CellOwnsStrut(self.StrutEndpointA(s), self.StrutEndpointB(s)) ? 1 : 0));

    //==
    // # Tiling a cell into world space
    //
    // The counts and the bounds fix the cell size; nothing stores it. Every node
    // position is `Min + (cellIndex + normalizedCoordinate) * cellSize` on each
    // axis, and that single spelling is what welds the lattice: the far-face
    // node of cell i and the near-face node of cell i + 1 both evaluate
    // (i + 1) * cellSize, so they land on the same world position exactly rather
    // than within a tolerance.

    // The world-space size of one cell on each axis: the bounds extent divided
    // by the repetition count. Cells are cubic only when the bounds are
    // proportional to the counts.
    CellSize(self: StrutLattice3D): Vector3D
        => Vector3D(
            (self.Bounds.Max.X - self.Bounds.Min.X) / self.Counts.X.ToNumber,
            (self.Bounds.Max.Y - self.Bounds.Min.Y) / self.Counts.Y.ToNumber,
            (self.Bounds.Max.Z - self.Bounds.Min.Z) / self.Counts.Z.ToNumber);

    // How many cells the lattice repeats in total.
    CellCount(self: StrutLattice3D): Integer
        => self.Counts.X.Max(0) * self.Counts.Y.Max(0) * self.Counts.Z.Max(0);

    // The integer coordinates of every cell, x fastest then y then z. A
    // non-positive count on any axis makes the lattice empty.
    Cells(self: StrutLattice3D): Array<IntegerVector3>
    {
        var columns = self.Counts.X.Max(0);
        var rows = self.Counts.Y.Max(0);
        var layers = self.Counts.Z.Max(0);
        var plane = columns * rows;
        return (plane * layers).MapRange(n =>
            IntegerVector3(n % columns, (n / columns) % rows, n / plane));
    }

    // The world position of a normalized cell coordinate inside a given cell.
    // The one place cell indices and normalized coordinates meet.
    NodePosition(self: StrutLattice3D, cell: IntegerVector3, node: Point3D): Point3D
    {
        var size = self.CellSize;
        return Point3D(
            self.Bounds.Min.X + (cell.X.ToNumber + node.X) * size.X,
            self.Bounds.Min.Y + (cell.Y.ToNumber + node.Y) * size.Y,
            self.Bounds.Min.Z + (cell.Z.ToNumber + node.Z) * size.Z);
    }

    // The world-space segment a strut of the cell occupies in a given cell.
    StrutSegment(self: StrutLattice3D, cell: IntegerVector3, s: LatticeStrut): Line3D
        => Line3D(
            self.NodePosition(cell, self.Cell.StrutEndpointA(s)),
            self.NodePosition(cell, self.Cell.StrutEndpointB(s)));

    //==
    // # Welding: which cell emits a shared strut
    //
    // `CellOwnsStrut` above states the rule for the infinite tiling. A finite
    // lattice keeps what the infinite one would drop whenever there is no next
    // cell to own it, so the far face of the last cell on an axis is closed
    // rather than left open.

    // True when this cell, and not the neighbour that shares a face with it,
    // emits the strut. The near-face copy wins wherever the neighbour exists.
    OwnsStrut(self: StrutLattice3D, cell: IntegerVector3, s: LatticeStrut): Boolean
    {
        var a = self.Cell.StrutEndpointA(s);
        var b = self.Cell.StrutEndpointB(s);
        return (OnFarFace(a.X) && OnFarFace(b.X) && cell.X + 1 < self.Counts.X).Not
            && (OnFarFace(a.Y) && OnFarFace(b.Y) && cell.Y + 1 < self.Counts.Y).Not
            && (OnFarFace(a.Z) && OnFarFace(b.Z) && cell.Z + 1 < self.Counts.Z).Not;
    }

    // True when this cell emits the node. A node on the far face of an axis
    // belongs to the next cell along, which describes it on its near face.
    OwnsNode(self: StrutLattice3D, cell: IntegerVector3, node: Point3D): Boolean
        => (OnFarFace(node.X) && cell.X + 1 < self.Counts.X).Not
        && (OnFarFace(node.Y) && cell.Y + 1 < self.Counts.Y).Not
        && (OnFarFace(node.Z) && cell.Z + 1 < self.Counts.Z).Not;

    // The struts one cell contributes, in the cell's own strut order.
    CellStruts(self: StrutLattice3D, cell: IntegerVector3): Array<Line3D>
        => self.Cell.Struts.FlatMap(s =>
            KeepSegment(self.OwnsStrut(cell, s), self.StrutSegment(cell, s)));

    // The nodes one cell contributes, in the cell's own node order.
    CellNodes(self: StrutLattice3D, cell: IntegerVector3): Array<Point3D>
        => self.Cell.Nodes.FlatMap(n =>
            KeepPoint(self.OwnsNode(cell, n), self.NodePosition(cell, n)));

    // Every strut of the lattice as a world-space segment, each shared strut
    // emitted exactly once and every shared node landing on one world position.
    // This is the single tiling path: the graded, trimmed and deformed variants
    // below all operate on the array this returns.
    Struts(self: StrutLattice3D): Array<Line3D>
        => self.Cells.FlatMap(c => self.CellStruts(c));

    // Every node of the lattice as a world-space position, each emitted exactly
    // once.
    Nodes(self: StrutLattice3D): Array<Point3D>
        => self.Cells.FlatMap(c => self.CellNodes(c));

    //==
    // # Readings on a tiled lattice
    //
    // The numbers an engineer asks of a lattice. Each walks the welded strut
    // list, so each counts a shared strut once.

    // How many struts the lattice has once welded.
    StrutCount(self: StrutLattice3D): Integer
        => self.Struts.Count;

    // How many nodes the lattice has once welded.
    NodeCount(self: StrutLattice3D): Integer
        => self.Nodes.Count;

    // The summed length of every strut: the length of wire the lattice is, and
    // the quantity relative density is proportional to.
    TotalLength(struts: Array<Line3D>): Number
        => struts.Reduce(0.0, (acc, s) => acc + s.Length);
```
